flux_evidence: runpodctl removed its only pod auto-stop/terminate flags (v2.12.0, 2026-08-27) five days after this skill's last check, and the PR revealed they never actually enforced the deadline in the first place — a financially load-bearing claim broke inside one cadence window on a CLI that ships every 1-3 weeks.

findings.claim: SKILL.md's 'Cost guards that actually work' section instructs setting --stop-after and --terminate-after on runpodctl pod create as 'the cost guards - a rename here has real financial consequence,' and states both were 'verified against runpodctl 2.3.0' / 're-verified live on 2026-08-23.'
findings.reality: Both flags were deleted in runpodctl v2.12.0 (2026-08-27, PR #330): the PR shows they were forwarded to the API but never enforced — pods kept running and billing past the deadline, with no way to read the timer back — so 'a flag that silently costs money is worse than no flag.' Passing either flag now fails immediately with 'unknown flag' and a non-zero exit; there is no CLI-level auto-stop until a backend fix (runpod/RunPod#5718) and a flag restoration (runpodctl#331) both land.
findings.fix_hint: SKILL.md 'Cost guards that actually work' (~L203-223), the pre-flight checklist item 8, and every failure-mode row mentioning --stop-after/--terminate-after need a rewrite: no such flag exists on current runpodctl, and even the version this skill verified against never made the timer fire. Promote the existing watchdog-script fallback to the primary guard.

new_techniques.what: RunPod's own golden-path 19 (live-verified 2026-07-13) attaches the same S3-synced data across three network volumes in three datacenters to one serverless endpoint (runpodctl serverless create --network-volume-ids v1,v2,v3, v2.4.0+), so workers schedule in whichever DC has free GPU stock instead of being pinned to one.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Directly mitigates the skill's stated 'volume is pinned to one datacenter, which narrows GPU availability' constraint for ComfyUI serverless deployments, at the cost of manual cross-DC sync discipline.
new_techniques.where_it_belongs: SKILL.md datacenter-lock caveat under 'Getting the weights there without burning GPU hours', or references/serverless-comfyui.md §4 — as an escape hatch with the sync-discipline caveat.

new_techniques.what: RunPod's own guide (updated 2026-09-08) recommends an external cron/scheduler hitting the RunPod REST API to create a pod, run the job, and explicitly call terminate, rather than relying on any CLI auto-stop timer.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: This is now the closest thing to a working, provable cost guard, given runpodctl's --stop-after/--terminate-after never fired and were removed outright in v2.12.0.
new_techniques.where_it_belongs: SKILL.md 'Cost guards that actually work' — as the primary replacement pattern alongside the existing watchdog-script advice.

new_techniques.why_it_matters: Gives a built-in, provable readiness check for the skill's own 'Running is not ready' smoke-test guidance, instead of hand-rolled polling.
new_techniques.where_it_belongs: SKILL.md 'Smoke test before you trust it' step 1, and the pre-flight checklist.
